title: River to Independence
summary: Follow Kuala Lumpur from the river confluence and early market streets to the civic landmarks around Merdeka Square.

stops.chapter: Begin where the Klang and Gombak rivers meet and where early Kuala Lumpur took shape.
Move into the old commercial centre around Medan Pasar and the town shaped by Yap Ah Loy.
See how one of the city's oldest Chinese institutions became part of the early urban fabric.
Trace the shift from a working wholesale market to a preserved cultural destination.
Return to the colonial civic centre through one of Kuala Lumpur's best-known administrative landmarks.
Finish at the field associated with the declaration of Malaysian independence in 1957.

title: Civic Architecture
summary: Compare the civic buildings, railway-era offices and courts that shaped Kuala Lumpur's institutional centre.

stops.chapter: Start from the open civic space that frames several major heritage buildings.
Examine the landmark administrative complex and its clock tower.
Compare the neighbouring former post office and its related architectural language.
Look for the contrasting brick-and-plaster treatment of the former railway offices.
Continue to the former municipal offices and theatre.
Compare another Hubback-era civic building across the historic core.
Finish with the long arcade and roof pavilions of the former Survey Office.

title: Trade & Communities
summary: Explore streets, places of worship and businesses that show how trading communities built everyday Kuala Lumpur.

stops.chapter: Begin at the old market square, once a centre of trade and town life.
Continue to Kuala Lumpur's oldest traditional Chinese temple.
See how the city's wholesale market evolved into today's Central Market.
Observe how modern banking and Art Deco design entered the commercial district.
Follow a street historically associated with South Indian Chettiar money-lenders.
Visit the Masjid India area and another important religious and commercial community.
Connect the district to one of Malaysia's longest-running jewellery businesses.
Finish among the businesses and street life associated with Jalan Melayu.

title: Modern KL Emerges
summary: Track the city's shift toward Art Deco, modern commerce and post-independence urban life.

stops.chapter: Start with a commercial cluster that includes an important Art Deco building.
Continue with a purpose-built 1930s bank and its modern urban details.
See the 1932 Oriental Building, once the tallest building in Kuala Lumpur.
Jump forward to early post-independence mass housing completed in 1964.
Finish with a 1970s commercial tower tied to Malay entrepreneurship.
